Sunrising
sŭn´rīz-ĭng
n. (the east; the quarter where the sun comes up; Hebrew mizrach hashshemesh)
A KJV compound rendering the Hebrew phrase toward the rising of the sun. Israel oriented itself by sunrise, and the tabernacle's gate faced it.

Biblical Definition

Sunrising is the KJV's way of naming the east by the thing that marks it. Israel's wilderness march is charted by it: “And they journeyed from Oboth, and pitched at Ijeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising” (Num 21:11). So is the trans-Jordan inheritance: “The two tribes and the half tribe have received their inheritance on this side Jordan near Jericho eastward, toward the sunrising” (Num 34:15). Moses fixes the cities of refuge by it: “Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising” (Deu 4:41), and describes the conquered land the same way, “the land of Og king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites, which were on this side Jordan toward the sunrising” (Deu 4:47). The east is where the tabernacle's one gate opened, where Eden's cherubim stood guard, where Ezekiel saw the glory return, and where the Lord Jesus said His coming would be as the lightning that shineth from the east even unto the west.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines sunrising as the first appearance of the sun above the horizon; the time of such appearance; and the east.

expand to see more

SUN-RISING, n. The first appearance of the sun above the horizon in the morning; also, the time of such appearance.

2. The east.

EAST, n. The point in the heavens where the sun is seen to rise at the equinox, or the corresponding point on the earth.

Key Scripture

Num 21:11 — "And they journeyed from Oboth, and pitched at Ijeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising."

Num 34:15 — "The two tribes and the half tribe have received their inheritance on this side Jordan near Jericho eastward, toward the sunrising."

Deu 4:41 — "Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising;"

Deu 4:47 — "And they possessed his land, and the land of Og king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites, which were on this side Jordan toward the sunrising;"

Modern Corruption

Direction in Scripture is read as incidental geography, while the east is consistently the quarter of entrance, exile and return.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Scripture's compass carries meaning. Man was driven out of Eden eastward and the cherubim were placed at the east of the garden; the tabernacle and the temple opened to the east; the glory departed by the east gate in Ezekiel 10 and returned by it in Ezekiel 43; and the wise men came from the east having seen a star. A reader who treats toward the sunrising as filler is skipping a thread the prophets deliberately picked up.

Deuteronomy 4:41 is worth noticing in its own right. Moses, forbidden to enter the land, spent part of his last strength severing three cities of refuge on the side of Jordan he could reach — toward the sunrising — so that a man who killed his neighbour unawares would have somewhere to run. He legislated mercy for a country he would never see. That is the character of the office, and Hebrews says the same of the patriarchs, who died in faith, not having received the promises.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mizrach (H4217), the place of rising, the east; from zarach (H2224), to rise or shine forth — the verb of Malachi 4:2, the Sun of righteousness shall arise.

expand to see more

Hebrew mizrach (H4217) — east, sunrising; Numbers 21:11, 34:15, Deuteronomy 4:41.

Hebrew zarach (H2224) — to rise, to shine forth; Malachi 4:2.

Hebrew shemesh (H8121) — sun; the second element of the Hebrew phrase.

Hebrew qedem (H6924) — east, also ancient time; the other Hebrew word for the quarter.

Greek anatole (G395) — the dayspring, the rising; Luke 1:78, the dayspring from on high.

Usage

"“In the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising” — the march, charted by dawn."

"“Then Moses severed three cities… toward the sunrising” — refuge, on the side he could reach."

"The east is the quarter of the gate, the exile, and the return."
